decisions.reason: As a secure document-storage feature for digital identity, it fits the firm's core knowledge base well, so management is likely to keep it and learn from early customer use rather than withdraw it quickly.

An identity-bound payment wallet is closely related to the firm's existing identity, payment and compliance capabilities, making it a plausible strategic complement despite still-limited market evidence.

Although authentication is central to the firm, an NFC-tag login product is more niche and may require more market education and partner uptake, so it has the highest withdrawal risk but is still worth retaining for another year.
A secure payment and wallet framework sits directly in the firm's established competence base and was given dedicated product visibility, which supports continued investment and commercialization.
This product is essentially the firm's strategic platform direction in super apps and secure ecosystems, so absorptive-capacity logic strongly favors keeping and refining it.

An application-shielding security library builds on the firm's long-standing security expertise and can be improved through its existing R&D knowledge, so management would likely keep it on the market.
